hypothesis: Prices keep drifting up for weeks after a clearly positive earnings surprise
test: Pre-registered event study (1358 events / 353 US tickers / ~4 quarters): surprise >=+5% arm vs neutral (+/-2%) control; entry next close; 20 sessions; 0.3% costs; bar = positive beats neutral in both halves at >=30 events/arm/half
verdict: FAILED - inverted on this universe. Positive-surprise beats averaged -0.4% (win 47%) while NEUTRAL reporters averaged +2.3% (win 60%) and won both halves. Caveats recorded: microcap EPS 'surprises' are tiny-denominator noise (median event was already a +7% beat; extremes reached +/-millions of percent) and the window is ~1 year - but on THIS universe buying the beat looks like buying the sell-the-news top. Classic large-cap PEAD does not transfer

hypothesis: Holding SPY only above its long-term trend avoids deep drawdowns cheaply
test: Pre-registered 10y test: 10-month SMA / 200-day SMA / 12m absolute momentum vs buy-and-hold; defensive bar = drawdown 25%+ shallower AND CAGR within 3pts in BOTH halves
verdict: NONE passed. SMA filters gave up ~7pts of CAGR/yr (8.2% vs 15.4%) for almost no drawdown relief (-23.4% vs -23.9%) - this decade's crashes were too fast for month-end signals which sold after the damage and re-bought late. 12m momentum came closest (DD -19.5% and only -3.4pts CAGR) but improved nothing in the first half. Insurance that costs 7%/yr and doesn't pay out is not insurance

hypothesis: Monthly rotation into the strongest ETFs captures the momentum premium after costs
test: Pre-registered 10y backtest (2016-2026; 39 ETFs; 120 months): 4 lookback/top-k variants vs SPY buy-and-hold AND equal-weight controls; bar = beat both controls in both halves at >=36 months/half
verdict: NONE passed. The 12m/top-3 variant posted 23.5% CAGR vs SPY's 15.4% - but LOST the first half (+1.33%/mo vs +1.45%) and won only the second (+2.66% - the 2024-26 metals/crypto regime); 3m won the first half and lost the second. Every variant had deeper drawdowns (-26% to -39% vs -24%) and fewer positive months than just holding SPY. Regime-chasing dressed as a premium; without the halves rule the 23.5% headline would have been traded
